title: 2 Data Center Stocks That Could Help Make You a Fortune
author: John Ballard
description: As hyperscalers invest heavily in data center infrastructure to support AI services, with Morgan Stanley projecting $1.4 trillion in capital spending by 2028, two data center stocks offer attractive valuations: Iren, which is building an AI cloud platform with vertically integrated capabilities and targeting $4 billion revenue by 2026, and Vertiv, which supplies power management and cooling systems to data centers with projected 20-22% annual revenue growth through 2030.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company is positioned as a leading AI cloud infrastructure provider with vertically integrated assets (land, power, construction), strong revenue growth trajectory ($1B to $4B by 2026), validated execution capability through Microsoft delivery, and analyst projections showing $10.7B adjusted operating profit by 2029 against $19B enterprise value, suggesting undervaluation.

Company benefits from increasing power demands in data centers with 24% YoY revenue growth, 22%+ operating margins, and management raising long-term guidance to 20-22% annual revenue growth through 2030. Wall Street expects 38% annualized earnings growth, and the company's end-to-end product portfolio deepens customer relationships.
Mentioned as a customer of Iren with a $9.7 billion five-year data center deal, indicating strong AI infrastructure investment but not the primary focus of the article.

title: Applied Digital vs. IREN: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares two AI infrastructure companies: Applied Digital (APLD) and IREN (IREN). Applied Digital shows stronger margins (22.38% vs 9.84%) and lower P/S ratio (13.1x vs 23.0x) but faces customer concentration risk with CoreWeave. IREN has secured major contracts with Microsoft ($9.7B) and Nvidia ($3.4B) and is pivoting from crypto mining to AI cloud services, though it reported a massive net loss of $702.6M. The author recommends IREN for patient investors due to its stronger contracted revenue base and blue-chip customer relationships, despite both companies currently losing money.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company shows strong revenue growth (183.7% YoY) and superior gross margins (22.38%), but faces significant customer concentration risk with CoreWeave, high debt-to-equity ratio (2.9x), and substantial net losses (-39.9% margin). Positive operational metrics offset by structural risks.

Despite massive net losses (-99.4% margin) and high debt ($7.98B), IREN has secured substantial long-term contracts with Microsoft ($9.7B) and Nvidia ($3.4B), providing revenue visibility. Nvidia's certification as reference-quality provider and successful pivot from crypto mining to AI infrastructure are significant positives. Author's recommendation favors this company.
Mentioned as Applied Digital's primary customer with full contract of flagship Polaris Forge 1 site, representing both revenue opportunity and concentration risk for APLD.
Mentioned as major customer of IREN with $9.7B five-year contract, indicating confidence in IREN's infrastructure capabilities.
Mentioned as IREN customer ($3.4B contract) and hardware supplier to both companies; certified IREN as reference-quality cloud provider, validating operational competence.

title: IREN Broadens Its AI Customer Base: Can Diversification Pay Off?
author: Na
description: IREN Limited is diversifying its AI cloud customer base away from heavy dependence on Microsoft and NVIDIA by signing $2.8 billion in contracts with Prometheus, Perplexity, and Together AI in July 2026. The company is experiencing stronger contract economics with three-year pricing up 125% and five-year pricing up 70%, though it faces risks from early-stage customers and shorter contracts. With 2026 capacity largely sold out, IREN is targeting broader customer expansion for 2027-2028.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company signed significant $2.8B in new contracts, achieved substantial pricing increases (125% for 3-year, 70% for 5-year contracts), and is successfully diversifying customer base away from concentration risk. However, sentiment is tempered by downward earnings revisions and premium valuation.

Strong Q2 2026 performance with $2.58B in revenues and $104B revenue backlog. Demonstrates significant scale with 1.5 GW active power and 3.7 GW contracted power, positioning it well in the competitive AI cloud market.
Solid Q2 2026 results with $582.3M group revenues and $3B ARR. Closed four major AI-cloud deals averaging over $1B each and raised contracted-power target to 5 GW, indicating strong growth momentum.

Mentioned as a major customer representing substantial portion of IREN's contracted revenues, but no specific performance data provided. Represents concentration risk that IREN is actively working to reduce.

title: NVIDIA Expands AI Infrastructure Capacity in Partnership With Australia’s Data Center Ecosystem
author: Nvidia
description: NVIDIA announced a major expansion of AI infrastructure in Australia through partnerships with local cloud providers and infrastructure companies including Firmus, Sharon AI, IREN, Megaport, ResetData, CDC, NEXTDC, and AirTrunk. The collaboration aims to deliver up to 2 gigawatts of capacity by 2027 using NVIDIA's DSX platform to support growing AI demand from startups, enterprises, and research organizations across the region.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: NVIDIA is expanding its AI infrastructure footprint in Australia through strategic partnerships, increasing addressable market for its DSX platform, accelerated computing products, and Nemotron models. This represents significant revenue growth opportunities and strengthens NVIDIA's position in the global AI infrastructure market.
IREN is leveraging its vertically integrated platform combined with NVIDIA's DSX architecture to deploy large-scale AI factories, including an 800-megawatt Bundey campus in South Australia.

Atlassian is leveraging NVIDIA's accelerated computing infrastructure and Nemotron open models to advance its Rovo AI product with semantic search capabilities, benefiting from expanded local AI infrastructure.

title: APLD Slides 36% in 3 Months: Should Investors Exit or Hold the Stock?
author: Zacks.Com
description: Applied Digital (APLD) has declined 35.6% over three months, significantly underperforming peers and the broader market. The company faces heavy capital requirements ($2.87B spent in fiscal 2026), rising leverage ($5.31B in debt obligations), and delayed revenue realization as most contracted capacity won't become operational until 2027-2028. Earnings estimates have been revised downward, and the stock trades at a premium valuation relative to peers. Zacks recommends selling due to unfavorable risk-reward dynamics.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock declined 35.6% in three months, underperforming sector and peers. Company faces significant near-term capital burden ($2.87B capex), high debt obligations ($5.31B), delayed revenue realization (most capacity operational in 2027-2028), downward earnings revisions, and premium valuation (P/B ratio 4.46X vs. industry 3.06X). Zacks assigns Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating.
